import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    size='Physical Activity Level',
    palette='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    sizes=(50, 800),    # Range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.7,          # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    edgecolor='w',      # White edge for better distinction of markers
    linewidth=0.5       # Line width for marker edges
)

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, Stress, and Physical Activity', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Customize ticks for better readability
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Position the legend outside the plot area
# The scatterplot automatically creates legends for both hue and size.
plt.legend(title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
